title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). L/K is a function field: L is finitely generated over K, and K has characteristic 0 (in the Longue Marche setting K is finitely generated over Q). U is a smooth model of L/K. E^{\bar L}_U denotes the arithmetic fundamental group pi_1(U, \bar L), with base point the chosen algebraic closure \bar L. Pi^{\bar L}_{U/K} is its geometric part.

Goal. A valuation ring V of L/K gives sections or decomposition data. Grothendieck wants to study Delta_V, the image of the inertia \bar I_V in pi_1^{geom}(U), which he expects to play the role of a 'loop group'. He asks to what extent distinct V give distinct Delta_V.

Tool: a good compactification. X is a proper model containing U. D = X - U is a normal crossings divisor with regular components D_i, i in I. For a point x of Supp D, take the henselization \tilde O_x of O_{X,x} (a strict point is intended), and let \tilde U_x be the inverse image of U in Spec \tilde O_x.

Equation (34). The local fundamental group fits into the exact sequence
1 -> T^{I(x)} -> pi_1(\tilde U_x, \bar L) -> Gal(\overline{k(x)}/k(x)) -> 1.
Here I(x) = {i : x in D_i} and T = T_\infty(\bar L^*) = \hat Z(1), the Tate module of the roots of unity. The algebraic closure \overline{k(x)} is induced by a chosen embedding of the fraction field \tilde K_x of \tilde O_x into \bar L.
This is the classical structure of the fundamental group of the complement of a normal crossings divisor in a henselian regular local scheme, in residue characteristic 0. It follows from Abhyankar's lemma and Zariski–Nagata purity (SGA 1 XIII, Grothendieck–Murre). All covers are tame, so the geometric part is the abelian group \hat Z(1)^{I(x)}.

Next, let V be a valuation ring of L/K whose center x on X lies in Supp D. Put S = Spec V, let \tilde S be its henselization inside \bar L, and let \tilde\eta be the generic point of \tilde S. The local homomorphism O_{X,x} -> V extends to \tilde O_x -> V^h by the universal property of henselization. Hence \tilde S -> X factors through \tilde T = Spec \tilde O_x, and \tilde\eta -> U factors through \tilde U_x.

Equation (35). The map N_V := pi_1(\tilde\eta) = Gal(\bar L / L^h_V), the decomposition group of V, to pi_1(U) factors as
N_V -> N_x := pi_1(\tilde U_x) -> pi_1(U).
The image of N_x in pi_1(U) is the decomposition group of x relative to \bar L. The study of N_V -> pi_1(U) thus splits into two parts:
- N_x -> pi_1(U): the next page conjectures this is injective, then the margin says this is visibly false when card I(x) != 1.
- N_V -> N_x: the next page conjectures this is open, with I_V -> I_x surjective, when the residue field of V is algebraic over K.

The page is a dévissage of the 'decomposition group of a valuation' into a local, normal-crossings part and a global part. It serves the higher-dimensional (birational / valuative) form of the section conjecture and the question of which valuations are detected by pi_1.
errors: No genuine error on this page; the factorization (35) and the exact sequence (34) are correct in characteristic 0 (tameness is automatic).

Minor imprecision: for (34) to have exactly Gal(k(x)) as quotient one needs the strict point/henselization conventions handled carefully. The text writes 'hensélisé' but marks 'point strict' on the previous page; with the plain henselization the quotient is Gal(\overline{k(x)}/k(x)) as written, which is consistent.
The injectivity guess made on the next page (that N_x -> pi_1(U) is injective) is retracted by Grothendieck himself in the margin for card I(x) > 1. This is not an error on this page itself.

ideas.what: Structure of pi_1 of the complement of a normal crossings divisor in a henselian regular local scheme: extension of Gal(k(x)) by \hat Z(1)^{I(x)}
ideas.modern_name: tame local fundamental group / Abhyankar's lemma + purity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck–Murre (tame fundamental group, 1971); SGA 1 Exp. XIII

ideas.what: Decomposition group of a valuation of L/K factors through the local fundamental group at its center on a normal crossings compactification
ideas.modern_name: decomposition/inertia groups of valuations in birational anabelian geometry; center of a valuation
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; used systematically by F. Pop and in work of Stix on sections and valuations
ideas.where_published: Theme of the 1983 letter to Faltings and Esquisse (section conjecture, birational variant), not this explicit factorization

ideas.what: Image Delta_V of the inertia of a valuation in pi_1^{geom}(U), viewed as analogue of a loop group; question whether distinct valuations give distinct Delta_V
ideas.modern_name: inertia subgroups of divisorial / general valuations; recovering valuations from Galois groups (local theory)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a program to compare inertia/decomposition groups of arbitrary valuations of L/K (not only divisorial ones) inside pi_1 of a fixed open model U, via the dévissage N_V -> N_x -> pi_1(U). He asks whether distinct valuations give distinct images Delta_V, as an analogue of loop groups. For non-birational, fixed-U pi_1 (as opposed to the absolute Galois group of L), this question seems only partially treated in the literature.
missed.quote: Dans quelle mesure des V distinctes définissent-elles des Δ_V distinctes ? ... (35) E_{η̃} → E_{Ũ_x} → E_U
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to higher-dimensional section conjecture variants: describing which sections or decomposition groups come from valuations of non-zero rank, and how their inertia sits in pi_1 of a higher-dimensional anabelian U. The injectivity question for local tame groups at multiple crossings is interesting for 'good' anabelian varieties.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is standard: the tame local pi_1 at a normal crossings point and the factorization of decomposition groups through the center. Its interest lies in the programmatic use for a higher-dimensional, valuative section conjecture and the 'loop group' analogy, which fits known Longue Marche themes.

In (34) the bar sits over T (\overline{T}^{I(x)}) and the superscript on the right term is \overline{k(x)}; this is consistent with the transcription.

'(dans \bar L choisi)' is an interlinear addition under '(dans un...)'. The phrase reads roughly '(de pt générique \tilde\eta)' and then 'une factorisation de \tilde\eta → U (composé \tilde\eta → η générique → U)'.
